analysis: The closest option has a sustained organisational-behaviour sequence through social psychology, leadership, communication, negotiation and strategy. Accounting and corporate finance replaces the spring offering conflict and adds costing, budgeting and control. Econometrics adds regression and instrumental variables, complementing behavioural statistics, survey research and qualitative methods. Public Policy Analysis, Public Economics and civic sociology provide public-sector context.

The innovation option develops product design, entrepreneurship, digital strategy, market research and stakeholder negotiation, together with life-cycle assessment and sustainability governance. Introduction to Economics and Consumer Product Design move to their offered first term. Negotiation and microeconomics replace renewable engineering and farming as stronger support for organisational decisions. Applied environmental courses retain a coherent supporting strand in product materials, circularity and responsible change.

The two options sustain different curricular emphases. The first focuses on behaviour, institutions and empirical inquiry. The second focuses on customer evidence, venture design, strategy and environmental decisions. None of the remaining exact interests needs a separate third direction.

Alignments reflect concrete shared topics or methods, such as survey design, social psychology, regression, qualitative inquiry, finance and negotiation. Dutch labour law, the specialist network and consultancy courses and both compulsory research units remain unpaired. The optional UCR research provision is outside the 180 EC schedule.

alignment.rationale: Both study accounting and financial decisions. Tilburg also teaches managing projects within and between organisations.
Both introduce economic reasoning about choices, markets and public intervention.
Both use regression to analyse empirical relationships. UCR also teaches instrumental variables and applies the methods to economics.
Both connect survey design, measurement and quantitative analysis. The UCR project studies leadership and social experience.
Both study motivation, teams, leadership and culture in organisations.
Both analyse strategic decisions. UCR focuses on negotiation, bargaining and relationships between parties.
Both use sociological theory to study institutions and social life.
Both use social psychology to study how people act in groups and respond to social influence.
Both introduce social-science research design, measurement and empirical analysis.
Both develop qualitative research design, data collection and interpretation. Tilburg applies these skills in its organisation studies sequence.
Both develop statistical analysis of social or behavioural data. UCR also applies multivariable models.
Both study organisational change. UCR focuses on planning for digital transformation.
Both examine entrepreneurship and innovation. UCR develops a venture idea through design and prototyping.
